questions.question: What does the acronym HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language. It is the standard markup language for creating web pages.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to create the largest heading on a page?
questions.explanation: The <h1> element defines the largest heading. Headings range from <h1> (most important) to <h6> (least important).

questions.question: Which attribute is used in the <a> tag to specify the destination URL?
questions.explanation: The href attribute specifies the URL of the page the link goes to.

questions.question: Which attribute is used to add alternative text to an image for accessibility?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text for an image if it cannot be displayed, and is essential for accessibility.

questions.question: Which CSS property is used to change the background color of an element?
questions.explanation: The background-color property sets the background color of an element.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid way to apply CSS to an HTML document?
options: Inline styles using the style attribute
All of the above are valid
questions.explanation: There is no <css> tag in HTML. CSS is applied via inline styles, internal <style> tags, or external <link> stylesheets.

questions.question: The <blockquote> element is used for which purpose?
options: Creating a long quotation that is indented
questions.answer: Creating a long quotation that is indented
questions.explanation: The <blockquote> element is used for longer quotations that typically appear indented. For short inline quotes, use <q>.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to create an ordered (numbered) list?
questions.explanation: The <ol> element defines an ordered list. Use <ul> for unordered lists.

questions.question: Which attribute is used to open a link in a new browser tab or window?
questions.explanation: The target attribute with the value "_blank" opens the linked document in a new tab or window.

questions.question: What is the correct HTML syntax for creating a mailto link?
questions.explanation: Mailto links use the <a> tag with href="mailto:email@address.com" to open the user's default email client.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to embed a video file on a webpage?
questions.explanation: The <video> element is used to embed video content in HTML documents.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid attribute for the <video> element?
questions.explanation: "playback" is not a valid attribute. Valid attributes include controls, autoplay, poster, muted, loop, and preload.

questions.question: What is the correct HTML for creating a checkbox in a form?
questions.explanation: The <input> element with type="checkbox" creates a checkbox input field.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to group related form elements together with a visual border?
questions.explanation: The <fieldset> element is used to group related elements in a form, often with a <legend> as a caption.

questions.question: Which method is used to attach an event listener to a DOM element in vanilla JavaScript?
questions.explanation: addEventListener() is the standard method for attaching event handlers to DOM elements.

questions.question: What does the JavaScript method `classList.toggle()` do when called on an element?
options: It permanently adds the specified class to the element
It permanently removes the specified class from the element
It adds the class if it's not present, and removes it if it is
It toggles the visibility (show/hide) of the element
It swaps the element's current class with a new one
questions.answer: It adds the class if it's not present, and removes it if it is
questions.explanation: The classList.toggle() method adds a class to an element if it doesn't exist, and removes it if it does. It's commonly used for hamburger menus and UI toggles.

questions.question: Which JavaScript method is used to select an HTML element by its id attribute?
questions.explanation: Both document.getElementById('id') and document.querySelector('#id') can select an element by id. getElementById is faster, but querySelector is more flexible.
